klv1_001: At 3:40 p.m., Ryuji Sakaguchi was just passing down the corridor when Kaori Miyama called him into the examination room.
klv1_002: Sitting on the edge of the exam table was a twenty-two-year-old woman. Her striking bright-red hair was tied into a lively side tail, and even though one hand was pressed over her lower abdomen, the moment she saw Sakaguchi walk in she sat straight up and flashed a social smile so sunny it practically came with its own sparkle filter.
klv1_003: "Oh, another doctor! Good afternoon—I'm Ikuyo Kita! Sorry for suddenly rushing into the ER in the middle of the day and causing trouble for both of you!"
klv1_004: Sakaguchi blinked slightly and gave a polite nod:
klv1_005: "Hello, I'm Ryuji Sakaguchi from Surgery. Is your stomach giving you a lot of trouble?"
klv1_006: Pressing her belly with one hand while waving her lit smartphone with the other, Kita spoke in a tone as breezy as if she were chatting about weekend plans:
klv1_007: "Honestly, it's nothing that dramatic! Maybe it's because I was rushing to revise lyrics at noon, drank an iced Americano on an empty stomach, and ate way too fast, so my stomach's been cramping on and off ever since. My band has ensemble rehearsal in Shimokitazawa at seven tonight, so I figured I'd swing by the hospital for some fast-acting painkillers and head over at a hundred percent—hss..."
klv1_008: Before she could finish, a sharp cramp hit; her practiced smile froze for half a second at the corner of her mouth before stubbornly curving right back up.
klv1_009: Standing in front of the X-ray lightbox, Kaori Miyama wasn't thrown off by her cheerful tone in the slightest, her brows slightly knit as she gave a concise briefing:
klv1_010: "Admitted twenty minutes ago. Subjective complaint of intermittent lower abdominal pain without a fixed location, no external trauma on inspection, and initial palpation showed no classic localized tenderness at McBurney's point. Just to be safe, I sent her for an upright plain abdominal film first."

klv1_013: Right in the center of the stark black-and-white abdominal X-ray—superimposed directly over the lower abdominal pelvic projection—lay an unmistakably sharp, elongated metallic shadow, down to the coiled spring at one end and the closed clasp at the tip.
klv1_014: Sakaguchi leaned in for a closer look:
klv1_016: Kita craned her neck curiously for a peek, and her eyes instantly flew wide:
klv1_018: Miyama turned around, fixing Kita with a sharp gaze:
klv1_019: "Ms. Kita, give us the whole truth. When did you swallow something like this?"
klv1_020: Kita waved both hands furiously, shaking her head like a rattle-drum:
klv1_021: "No way, Dr. Miyama!! I'm twenty-two years old, not a three-year-old toddler—how could I possibly swallow a safety pin?! Even if I wolfed down my convenience-store rice ball at lunch, biting into an iron pin would definitely have cracked my teeth, right?!"
klv1_022: Pointing at the film, she tried her best to put on a polite yet aggrieved smile to smooth things over:
klv1_023: "Um... could Radiology have accidentally mixed up someone else's film just now? Or maybe a pin happened to stick to the camera lens or something?"
klv1_024: Miyama glanced at the name, age, and timestamp printed in the corner of the film, briskly ruling out any wishful thinking:
klv1_025: "Name: Ikuyo Kita, age twenty-two, taken at 15:32. Metal hardware on her outer garments was cleared per protocol before the exposure—there's no chance the film was mixed up."
klv1_027: "That's so weird... All I had today was an iced Americano and one rice ball—I swear I never put a safety pin anywhere near my mouth!"
klv1_028: Staring at the metallic shadow sitting dead center over her lower abdomen, Miyama's expression turned completely grave.
klv1_029: "Whether you swallowed it by accident or forgot how it happened, two objective facts remain: first, the plain abdominal film captured a sharp metallic foreign body projected over your lower abdomen; second, you are sitting in the ER right now with acute abdominal pain of unknown origin. klv1_030: Without a trace of hesitation, she turned straight toward Sakaguchi:
klv1_031: "Dr. Sakaguchi, we need to prep this case immediately as an acute abdomen with a suspected foreign body. You have more open laparotomy experience than I do—you take primary surgeon, and I'll scrub in as your first assistant."
klv1_032: Hearing the words "primary surgeon," the radiant smile on Kita's face at the edge of the exam table finally cracked.
klv1_033: "W-Wait a second! Doctors, when you say 'prep this case'... don't tell me you mean cutting me open?!"
klv1_034: Signing the emergency transfer slip, Miyama answered calmly:
klv1_035: "Based on the current imaging and symptoms, we have to prepare for surgery."
klv1_036: Sakaguchi took the chart, scanned her vital signs and initial bloodwork screen, and made the call steadily:
klv1_037: "Agreed. Notify the OR to set up an emergency table immediately."
klv1_038: Kita sprang straight up from the edge of the exam table:
klv1_039: "Eeeh?! Today?! I still have band rehearsal for our new song at the livehouse at seven tonight, and we have a joint gig next week!"

klv1_042: Emergency prep at Hoshimi Hospital moved like clockwork.

klv1_047: "...N-No way, is this for real...? Just this morning I was taking outfit selfies before leaving the house—how am I suddenly getting wheeled in to have my stomach cut open...?"

klv1_052: Clutching the front of her transport gown with both hands, Kita glanced reflexively at the male lead surgeon Sakaguchi a few paces away; her cheeks flared crimson as she tried politely in a tiny voice to negotiate:

klv1_057: Biting her lip, she turned half away, ears burning red as she untied the transport gown and handed it to Rumi; then she took a deep breath, bent down to slide her last pair of light-colored cotton panties down her legs, balled them up in her hand, and passed them into the basket.

klv1_091: "...Wait, no, maybe it doesn't hurt...? Eh... I-I don't know..."

klv1_095: "B-Because when I saw the pin fall out just now, I was so happy it suddenly felt like my stomach didn't hurt at all anymore... b-but the moment you asked so seriously, Dr. Miyama, it started feeling all twitchy and weird inside my lower belly again..."

klv1_098: At those words, alarm bells went off wildly inside Kita's head as survival instinct and twenty-two years of finely honed social reflexes fired at once—craning her neck up, she forced out a picture-perfect smile ten times brighter than before:

klv1_180: For the first time in her life, this social natural—whose quick tongue could charm her way through school, part-time shifts, and livehouses alike—learned what it felt like to have her own words seal off every last escape route.

klv1_218: Following the anatomical planes unhurriedly, Sakaguchi gently ran the terminal ileum and adjacent lower small-bowel segments centimeter by centimeter:
klv1_219: "Right. Let's inspect each segment in order and make sure we don't miss an occult diverticulum."
klv1_220: Though she felt zero sharp pain, the subtle, muffled tugging deep inside her abdomen—the unmistakable sensation of gloved hands gently sliding and drawing things aside inside her own belly—made Kita's skin prickle behind the drape as she strained her ears to eavesdrop on the two surgeons:
klv1_221: "Ugh... feeling something gently pulling back and forth inside my stomach is so weird... U-Um, Dr. Miyama, if my appendix isn't swollen and my small intestine isn't torn, don't tell me there's really nothing wrong inside me at all...?"
klv1_222: Sakaguchi's tone remained warm and unhurried:
klv1_223: "Don't rush to call the findings for us yet, Ms. Kita. We still need to finish checking the sigmoid colon and pelvis—slow your breathing down a little."
klv1_224: Holding the abdominal wall retractor at a steady angle, Miyama glanced at Sakaguchi above her surgical mask and lowered her voice a fraction toward her partner:
klv1_225: "...You really don't rattle easily. Even after I framed the case so urgently earlier, you didn't rush the exploration."
klv1_226: "Once we commit to opening the abdomen, we owe it to her to inspect the lower abdomen and pelvis thoroughly—missing a hidden corner is what would truly make the incision pointless. Help me expose the sigmoid colon and deep pelvis."
klv1_228: Lower small intestine and ileocecal region—bowel wall pink and supple, without a trace of puncture or perforation.
klv1_229: Sigmoid colon and rectouterine pouch—serosa smooth and intact, free of inflammatory adhesions or diverticulitis.
klv1_230: Bilateral pelvic adnexa—spotless, without even a drop of abnormal effusion or exudate.
klv1_231: For a moment the operating room fell quiet save for the steady pulse of the monitor.
klv1_232: Pausing his exploration, Sakaguchi looked up across the table at his first assistant:
klv1_233: "Exploration of the lower bowel loops, appendix, and pelvis is complete. Zero organic pathology identified—a textbook negative laparotomy."
klv1_234: Miyama gazed down beneath the surgical light at the impeccably healthy abdominal viscera, silent for two seconds.
klv1_235: There was no wounded pride, nor any awkwardness over losing face. Shoulders that had been taut all afternoon slowly settled as, behind her mask, she let out a quiet, genuinely relieved breath:
klv1_239: Miyama raised her clear, earnest eyes, her voice completely free of pretense:
klv1_241: Hardly had the words fallen when dead silence held behind the cranial drape for one full second—followed by an outraged protest loud enough to nearly knock her blue surgical cap askew—
klv1_242: "WAIT JUST A SECOND—!! What do you mean 'Thank goodness, she's completely healthy'?! My stomach is still cut wide open right now, isn't it?! Did you seriously open up my belly, rummage around inside, and say 'Thank goodness, completely healthy' straight to my internal organs in front of me?!!"
klv1_243: Faced with the patient's on-the-spot meltdown, Miyama showed zero guilt; instead, she answered across the drape in a tone of a hundred percent sincere relief, as if nothing could be more self-evident:
klv1_244: "Would you rather we had found a bowel perforation or suppurative appendicitis inside you? Confirming with our own eyes that there is no organic lesion at all is obviously the best possible news today."
klv1_245: Tears glistening at the corners of her eyes, Kita wailed:
klv1_246: "W-Well, when you put it like that, sure... but I was just a healthy band vocalist who came in for painkillers to begin with!! Boohoo... now that you've confirmed I'm super healthy, please sew me back up quick, both of you!!"
klv1_247: Looking at Miyama's utterly earnest relief while listening to the spirited protest from behind the drape, Sakaguchi couldn't help letting out a quiet chuckle as he accepted the needle holder from Mika Nakai:
klv1_248: "You heard the patient hurrying us along. Come on, First Assistant—sponge and instrument count, let's prepare to close."
klv1_250: As the numbness of the spinal block gradually wore off from her lower body, Kita lay flat in bed changed back into a light-colored hospital gown. Though sterile dressings covered her lower abdomen and she couldn't twist around yet, her spirits were visibly livelier than before surgery—holding her freshly returned smartphone up with both hands and sighing dramatically over the exploding '99+' unread messages in her band group chat.
klv1_251: The instant she spotted Kaori Miyama and Ryuji Sakaguchi pushing open the ward door, Kita turned her head and puffed out her cheeks in plaintive protest:
klv1_252: "Aaah—Dr. Miyama, Dr. Sakaguchi! You two really have the nerve to walk in for rounds looking completely calm!"
klv1_253: Stepping up to the bedside, Miyama carefully checked her post-op pulse, lower-limb sensory recovery, and incision dressing before delivering a composed clinical update:
klv1_254: "Your vital signs are steady, and the incision dressing is clean and dry. Since organic pathology was thoroughly ruled out intraoperatively, this afternoon's abdominal pain was most likely a transient intestinal spasm triggered by drinking an iced Americano on an empty stomach plus pre-rehearsal tension."
klv1_255: Lowering her phone, Kita stared up at the ceiling half-laughing, half-crying:
klv1_256: "I lay on that operating table with my eyes wide open listening to every single word from start to finish!! First I got wheeled into the OR over a safety pin stuck in my underwear waistband, then I didn't even get put to sleep—I just lay there wide awake behind a green cloth listening to you rummage through my stomach and cheerfully announce 'Thank goodness, she's completely healthy'! Where on earth do you find an ER experience that absurd?!"
klv1_257: Miyama mulled that over with utmost seriousness for half a second:
klv1_258: "Compared with sleeping through everything in a haze, doesn't hearing with your own ears while wide awake that you're completely healthy put your mind at ease right on the spot—"
klv1_259: Quick on the uptake, Sakaguchi cleared his throat lightly to cut that line of reasoning short:
klv1_260: "Dr. Miyama, there's no need to elaborate on that particular reassurance."
klv1_262: "It doesn't put my mind at ease ONE BIT!! How am I supposed to explain this in our band group chat?! Gotoh-san was already so terrified in the chat earlier she offered to fold a thousand paper cranes for me—if I text them 'Sorry, the safety pin was actually stuck in my underwear, but I stayed wide awake listening to the doctors cut my belly open to confirm I'm super healthy,' everyone at the livehouse next week is gonna laugh at me for the rest of my life!!"
klv1_264: "Just tell everyone you were kept overnight for observation with acute intestinal spasms. Rest flat tonight, and you'll be back at rehearsal before long."
klv1_265: Though Kita still muttered under her breath about how 'hardcore this hospital's checkups are,' remembering the unmistakable sincerity in Miyama's quiet 'Thank goodness' at the operating table soon brought a bright, sunny smile back to her face as she waved at them both:
klv1_266: "All right, all right—hearing Dr. Miyama breathe that sigh of relief behind the curtain earlier, I could tell both of you were genuinely worried something bad might happen to me! Just remember to help me come up with a cooler-sounding excuse for missing rehearsal during morning rounds tomorrow, okay!"
klv1_267: Shortly after leaving the ward, while Sakaguchi stopped by the nurses' station to sign post-op orders, Asuka Shiromiya walked down the quiet early-evening hallway cradling a stack of administrative folders and paused beside Kaori Miyama at the vending machines.
klv1_268: With nobody else around, Asuka dropped the hospital director formalities, her tone as familiar as if they were back in a university clubroom:
klv1_269: "I heard you performed an emergency exploratory laparotomy this afternoon on a band vocalist who turned out to be completely healthy?"
klv1_270: Pressing the button for a warm canned tea, Miyama didn't even turn around:
klv1_271: "There were clinical grounds at the time. The X-ray had a foreign-body artifact, and the patient couldn't give a coherent account of her pain."
klv1_273: "I didn't say your judgment was wrong."
klv1_274: Miyama turned her head to cast a sidelong look at her old classmate:
klv1_275: "Then why did Madam Director come all the way over here?"
klv1_276: "To check whether a certain someone was spiraling into self-criticism and hiding in a corner skipping dinner."
klv1_277: Holding the warm can, Miyama gave a quiet huff:
klv1_279: Asuka chuckled, patted the back of her hand, and softened her voice a touch:
klv1_280: "Good. ...The patient is safe and sound, and nothing matters more than that. Go get dinner once you wrap up, Kaori."
klv1_281: A few minutes later, Asuka headed off, and Sakaguchi walked down the hallway after finishing the post-op orders.
klv1_282: Dusk was deepening outside the window. Standing by the glass with the unopened warm tea can still in her hand, Miyama seemed to be quietly reviewing every step at the operating table that afternoon—from that crisp 'Ding.' to the moment she had pressed too hard in her urgency to get a clear palpation answer.
klv1_283: Seeing Sakaguchi approach, Miyama turned toward him and spoke up first:
klv1_287: Looking him straight in the eye, Miyama spoke calmly and candidly:
klv1_288: "This afternoon at the operating table, the moment that safety pin dropped out—if you had used your authority as primary surgeon to overrule me and cancel the operation on the spot, I would have tried to stop you."
klv1_290: "I know. That's why I wanted to hear your reasoning all the way through."
klv1_291: Miyama blinked slightly, then pressed the corner of her lips together ever so faintly.
klv1_292: She glanced down at the tea can in her hand before raising her eyes squarely to Sakaguchi again. The aloof, appraising edge she usually carried softened, replaced by genuine professional recognition:
klv1_293: "Plenty of surgeons more worried about liability would have jumped at the excuse to send the patient home the moment the pin turned up in her clothes—and written me off as overreacting. ...Thank you for not brushing me off today, and for listening to the full clinical reasoning behind my call."
klv1_294: Sakaguchi's expression was warm and steady:
klv1_295: "You were the attending physician who examined her first, and the blind spot you pointed out was real. Whenever you have solid clinical grounds, of course I'll listen seriously."
klv1_296: Miyama paused for a heartbeat before a faint, clear smile touched the corner of her lips:
klv1_297: "...Right. With your word on that, the next time a thorny case comes into the ER, I'll call you straightaway."
klv1_298: Sakaguchi smiled with a touch of light teasing:
klv1_299: "Of course I'll listen. Next time we palpate on the operating table, though, remember to hold back a little before pressing deep—even the chattiest patient can't tell what hurts anymore once you press like that."
klv1_300: The tips of Miyama's fair ears warmed almost imperceptibly, yet instead of bristling, she nodded frankly:
klv1_301: "...I really was too impatient for a definitive answer on that press. Noted—I'll do better next time."
klv1_302: Looking out at the night sky beyond the window, Sakaguchi spoke gently:
klv1_303: "The path there took a few twists, sure, but confirming with our own eyes that she's completely healthy is hardly a bad outcome."
klv1_304: Miyama let out a soft breath, a rare, relaxed smile touching her lips:
klv1_305: "True enough. Far better than letting her go sing halfway through a set only to come back in an ambulance."
klv1_306: Popping the tab on her warm tea can, Miyama gave Sakaguchi a composed, respectful nod:
klv1_307: "Thank you for taking the lead at the table today, Dr. Sakaguchi. It seems the Director's praise for your surgical record wasn't mere politeness after all—see you in the OR next time."
klv1_308: Watching her brisk figure turn down the hall toward the on-call room, Sakaguchi could tell unmistakably that this eminent surgeon's daughter—who had kept a cool, appraising distance since their very first meeting—had for the first time genuinely placed him on her list of clinical partners she could debate seriously and share responsibility with.
choice_1_a: "Since we found the pin, let's cancel the surgery for now and pack up."
choice_1_b: "Finding the pin outside her body actually leaves her original abdominal pain unexplained."
choice_2_a: "Whenever you have solid clinical grounds, of course I'll listen seriously."
choice_2_b: "Next time you palpate, go easy on the pressure—you pressed her completely dizzy."
choice_2_c: "Confirming she's completely healthy in the end is hardly a bad outcome."
